chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandi, from Abu Waki', from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Harith al-A'war, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no good in lying, whether in seriousness or in jest, nor in one of you promising his child something then failing to fulfill it. Indeed, lying leads to immorality, and immorality leads to the Hellfire. One of you will keep on lying until it is said: "He lied and committed immorality." And one of you will keep on lying until there does not remain in his heart even the space of a needle's worth of truthfulness, and so he is called a liar before God.

key_terms.الفجور: Immorality, wickedness (al-fujur) - a comprehensive term for sinful deviations
key_terms.الكذب: Lying, falsehood (al-kadhib) - any deliberate utterance contrary to the truth
key_terms.صدق: Truthfulness, sincerity (sidq) - the opposite of lying, a fundamental moral virtue in Islam

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the consequences of lying in Islam?
ai.summary: In this teaching from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam Ali (AS) delivers a stern warning against lying in all its forms, addressing his audience of believers in the mosque of Kufa. He prohibits lying whether serious or joking, and particularly condemns making false promises to children. He explains the spiritual mechanism by which habitual lying escalates to immorality and ultimately leads to the Hellfire, eroding all truthfulness from the heart until one is designated a liar in God's record.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
